newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market steady, trading heads for lull.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market steady, trading heads for lull.

text.p: Vietnam's rice market was steady this week as export demand held firm, but traders said they saw business slowing in the weeks ahead because the main rice-growing area was now between crops.
"It's that period between crops when there's not much rice left," said one trader. "So stable demand has kept prices very steady."
Five percent broken grade was offered at $255 per tonne, FOB Saigon Port, unchanged from last week. Ten percent broken was put at $245-$250 a tonne, down from $250-$253 a week ago.
Around 17 vessels, half of them bound for Africa, were loading in Saigon Port, and dealers said new deals for shipments to Africa and Indonesia were likely in the coming weeks.
The General Statistic Office said in a report earlier this week that rice exports totalled 500,000 tonnes in June.
Traders, however, see exports dropping to 300,000-400,000 tonnes this month due to slowing demand and stockpiling of quality winter-spring rice by farmers in the Mekong Delta.
Unusually dry weather is expected to affect the volume of the summer-autumn crop and quality could also be affected by flooding in the delta, which usually starts in September.

June exports took the total for the first half of this year to 1.86 million tonnes, 46 percent more than in the same period of 1996. The government is targeting exports of 3.5 million tonnes for 1997.
